protocol.instrument_name: Pharmacist Resupply of Oral Contraceptive Pills Pilot - Western Australian Protocol
protocol.instrument_version: No version number or date printed on the document
protocol.legal_basis: Structured Administration and Supply Arrangement (SASA): the dispensing record for resupply must not list the previous medical practitioner or nurse practitioner in the 'prescriber' field; the pharmacist's name and Healthcare Provider Identifier-Individual (HPI-I) must be included for My Health Record transmission; a documented patient request to withhold transmission 'serves as a justifiable reason for not meeting condition 4(m) of the SASA'. Record keeping of supply must be kept for at least 2 years, in accordance with Part 12 of the Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016 (WA) (p.5).
protocol.supervision_model: Pilot authorisation as printed: 'This protocol provides a framework for pharmacists authorised to resupply oral contraceptive pills to eligible patients' (p.1); supply is recorded under the SASA in the pharmacist's own name with their HPI-I (p.5). The document does not use the terms 'collaborative' or 'autonomous'.
protocol.scope_summary: Western Australian pilot protocol for pharmacist resupply of oral contraceptive pills (OCP). Program Scope WA criteria A-K define the scope: age 16-39 years inclusive; combined oral contraception (COC) and progestogen-only contraception (POP) oral dosage forms; OCP initiated by a GP or Nurse Practitioner and stabilised minimum 2 years continuously; OCP review with a medical practitioner or nurse practitioner minimum every 2 years; TGD people presumed female at birth included; pill break maximum 2 weeks continuously; re-supply one manufacturer's pack or maximum up to 12 months; high dose estrogen (50 microg ethinylestradiol) not permitted; permitted estrogens and progestogens listed with excluded substances; and K. Exclusion criteria (UKMEC Category 3 & 4 contraindications) for COC and POP. Explanatory notes (pp.4-5), Pharmacist assessment (p.5), Documentation and communication (pp.5-6), Non-pharmacological and self-care advice (p.6) and Fees and charges (p.6) support the pathway; Attachment 1 (p.7) is a summary table for OCP whose rows were not present in the text extraction.

inclusion.text: B. Dosage forms Combined oral contraception and progestogen-only contraception. Dosage forms other than oral formulations excluded.

C. OCP history OCP initiated by a General Practitioner or a Nurse Practitioner and has been stabilised for minimum 2 years continuously. Different OCP or hormones excluded on protocol medicines list are not permitted.
D. OCP review A thorough review of the OCP with a medical practitioner or nurse practitioner. Minimum every 2 years.

E. Transgender and gender diverse people presumed female at birth - Included, and professional obligations apply. (Explanatory note E, page 4: 'The resupply of OCP is permitted for TGD individuals, provided all other protocol conditions are met.')

F. Pill break Maximum 2 weeks continuously. (Explanatory note F, page 5: 'Pill breaks should not exceed 2 weeks consecutively, with inactive pills not considered part of the pill break in this context. The total duration of pill breaks should not surpass 4 weeks within a 12-month period.')
G. Re-supply quantity One manufacturer's pack, or maximum up to 12 months.
I. Permitted estrogens Estradiol; Ethinylestradiol (See attachment 1)
J. Permitted progestogens Levonorgestrel; Norethisterone; Drospirenone; Nomegestrol; Desogestrel; Dienogest; Gestodene (See attachment 1)

exclusion.text: H. High dose estrogen (50 microg of ethinylestradiol) - Not permitted
I. Excluded - estetrol, mestranol
J. Excluded - Cyproterone

[COC and POP] K. Exclusion criteria: If drug interactions are identified. For example, prescription/non-prescription medications (CYP 3A4/5 inducers such as carbamazepine, corticosteroids, modafinil, phenobarbital, phenytoin, rifampicin, St John's wort)

diagnosis_pathways.name: Pharmacist resupply of OCP - assessment, supply and follow-up

steps.description: Confirm the Program Scope WA criteria before resupply: A. Age range 16-39 years (inclusive); B. Dosage forms combined oral contraception and progestogen-only contraception (dosage forms other than oral formulations excluded); C. OCP history - OCP initiated by a General Practitioner or a Nurse Practitioner and has been stabilised for minimum 2 years continuously (different OCP or hormones excluded on protocol medicines list are not permitted); D. OCP review - a thorough review of the OCP with a medical practitioner or nurse practitioner, minimum every 2 years; E. Transgender and gender diverse people presumed female at birth - included, and professional obligations apply; F. Pill break - maximum 2 weeks continuously; G. Re-supply quantity - one manufacturer's pack, or maximum up to 12 months; H. High dose estrogen (50 microg of ethinylestradiol) - not permitted. Before resupplying, pharmacists should verify the previous prescription by sighting it or through other physical or electronic records (e.g., My Health Records, dispensing records).

gates.criterion: C. OCP initiated by a General Practitioner or a Nurse Practitioner and has been stabilised for minimum 2 years continuously
B. Dosage forms other than oral formulations excluded
H. High dose estrogen (50 microg of ethinylestradiol) - Not permitted

steps.description: Check the K. Exclusion criteria (including UKMEC Category 3 & 4 contraindications) against both the Combined oral contraception (COC) column and the Progestogen-only contraception (POP) column: current or previous history of breast cancer (including carrier of known gene mutations, e.g. BRCA); hepatocellular adenoma, or malignant liver tumour; severe (decompensated) cirrhosis; potentially pregnant; STI screening is indicated; unexplained and un-investigated vaginal bleeding or acute, severe menstrual bleeding; drug interactions (e.g. prescription/non-prescription medications (CYP 3A4/5 inducers such as carbamazepine, corticosteroids, modafinil, phenobarbital, phenytoin, rifampicin, St John's wort)); COC-only criteria (migraine with/without aura; prolonged immobilisation; plus the page 3 list); POP-only criterion (ischaemic heart disease, stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA) that develops during use of POP). Table note: conditions that require immediate referral - refer the patient to their regular GP with a copy of the assessment. See also UKMEC April 2016 (Amended September 2019) and UKMEC April 2016 Summary Sheet (Amended September 2019).

gates.criterion: Any K. Exclusion criteria present (including UKMEC Category 3 & 4 contraindications)

steps.description: Clinical Measurements: For COC, measure the patient's blood pressure and BMI.

gates.criterion: EXC-16: Hypertension (systolic blood pressure 140mmHg or higher, diastolic blood pressure 90mmHg or higher), including adequately controlled hypertension (K. Exclusion criteria, page 3)
EXC-26: Body mass index (BMI) ≥ 35kg/m2 (K. Exclusion criteria, page 3)

steps.description: Confidentiality: consultations must be conducted in a private room to maintain confidentiality; it should not be seen or heard by a person not involved in the consultation. Consent: documented informed consent must be obtained from the patient (this can include financial consent (costs to the patient), consent to access medical records, and consent for referral). Risk Assessment: assess the patient's adherence, smoking status, adverse effects to OCP, changes in bleeding pattern, changes in health, new medications, and potential pregnancy.

gates.criterion: Documented informed consent must be obtained from the patient
EXC-14: Age 35 years or older and current smoker or recently quit smoking in the last 12 months (including nicotine vaping) (K. Exclusion criteria, page 3)
EXC-10: If drug interactions are identified (K. Exclusion criteria, page 2)

steps.description: Risk Categories: patients with UKMEC category 3 and 4 risks are considered high risk and must be referred; category 2 risks can be considered, and pharmacists should exercise professional judgement when multiple category 2 conditions are present. References: refer to UKMEC, Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook (AMH), product information, and other relevant references. Social and Sexual Health Discussion: discuss social and sexual health issues as appropriate; refer confidentially when required. Adherence and Satisfaction Check: check the patient's adherence and satisfaction with OCP; offer contraceptive counselling to explore other options as appropriate, e.g., LARCs.

gates.criterion: Patients with UKMEC category 3 and 4 risks are considered high risk and must be referred

steps.description: Resupply the OCP (oral contraceptive pills) within the quantity limits: G. Re-supply quantity - one manufacturer's pack, or maximum up to 12 months. Patients aged 16-17 years can have up to 4 months resupplied as an extension to their original prescription, provided other protocol conditions are met (given the potential health and social risk factors these patients should have more frequent contraception reviews and be encouraged to engage regularly with a GP; a thorough review is essential, and a new prescription must be issued for subsequent supplies). Patients aged 18-39 years can have up to 12 months of OCP resupplied at once, guided by the patient's preference and the pharmacist's assessment. Other conditions must be considered when determining the quantity.

gates.criterion: Other conditions must be considered when determining the quantity (for example, a patient turning 40 years-of-age in a month should not be given a full 12-month resupply)
The review date must be considered during resupply, ensuring that the quantity resupplied only allows for the continuation of OCP within the 2-year period

steps.description: Documentation and communication: the pharmacist must create and maintain a comprehensive clinical record of the consultation, including patient identifiers and consent given; date of consultation and name of pharmacist who undertook the consultation; clinical information relevant to the resupply (e.g., medical and OCP history, BMI, BP, pregnancy status, STI risks); clinical opinion reached by the pharmacist, as well as the actions and management plan; details of the OCP supplied (generic name, strength, and quantity); counselling and advice given to the patient; any referrals made to another healthcare professional with patient's consent. A copy of this record should be provided to the patient and, if necessary, their regular medical practitioner. Record keeping of supply must be kept for at least 2 years, in accordance with Part 12 of the Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016. The dispensing record for resupply must not list the previous medical practitioner or nurse practitioner in the 'prescriber' field; instead the name of the pharmacist who undertook the consultation must be used, and their Healthcare Provider Identifier-Individual (HPI-I) number must be included alongside other critical information (e.g. patient's IHI) for My Health Record transmission. The pharmacy dispensing software must be configured to enable the details of the supply to be uploaded to My Health Record.

A referral should be initiated only with the patient's consent. Where practical, it should be directed to the patient's regular GP or another GP within the same practice. This approach helps maintain the continuity of care for the patient. Referral destinations named in the protocol: regular medical practitioner or health service (patients not eligible for resupply); GP, sexual health clinic, or health service (patients under 16 years, or 40 years and over); regular GP with a copy of the assessment (conditions that require immediate referral); medical review (patient turning 40 years-of-age in a month); alternative contraception options (patient frequently takes pill breaks).

Non-pharmacological and self-care advice: provide Consumer Medicines Information and/or a Self-Care Fact Card, and appropriate counselling on the OCP supplied - Instructions (how to take the OCP and recognise active/inactive pills); Side Effects (what side effects to expect, potential drug interactions, signs of VTE and what to do if it is suspected); Missed Pill (what to do in the event of a missed pill, with instructions specific to the OCP resupplied, additionally emergency contraception options available if required); Adherence (reiterate the importance of adherence and avoiding starting/stopping the pill); Blood Pressure Monitoring (the patient's blood pressure should be monitored at least at 12 monthly intervals); GP Review (patients should engage with a regular GP and be reviewed at least every two years); Cervical Screening (available for women from the age of 25 and recommended every 5 years); Breast Checks (recommended for women who have a personal or family history of breast cancer - patients should seek GP advice regarding the frequency and type of screening); STI Screening (recommended for anyone who is sexually active and engaging in unprotected sex).

Follow-up requirements: patients on OCP should have a medical review at least every 2 years and the quantity resupplied must only allow continuation of OCP within the 2-year period; blood pressure should be monitored at least at 12 monthly intervals; patients should engage with a regular GP and be reviewed at least every two years; patients aged 16-17 years should have more frequent contraception reviews and be encouraged to engage regularly with a GP; cervical screening every 5 years from the age of 25; breast checks for women with a personal or family history of breast cancer; STI screening for anyone who is sexually active and engaging in unprotected sex.

treatments.drug: Oral contraceptive pills (combined oral contraception and progestogen-only contraception)
treatments.dose: Resupply of the OCP the patient has been stabilised on (no dose printed in this document; product strengths are in Attachment 1, page 7)
treatments.max_quantity: One manufacturer's pack, or maximum up to 12 months (G. Re-supply quantity); patients aged 16-17 years: up to 4 months as an extension to their original prescription; patients aged 18-39 years: up to 12 months of OCP resupplied at once, guided by the patient's preference and the pharmacist's assessment
treatments.quantity_to_supply: One manufacturer's pack, or maximum up to 12 months
treatments.notes: B. Dosage forms - combined oral contraception and progestogen-only contraception; dosage forms other than oral formulations excluded. C. OCP history - different OCP or hormones excluded on protocol medicines list are not permitted. H. High dose estrogen (50 microg of ethinylestradiol) - not permitted. I. Permitted estrogens: estradiol, ethinylestradiol (excluded - estetrol, mestranol). J. Permitted progestogens: levonorgestrel, norethisterone, drospirenone, nomegestrol, desogestrel, dienogest, gestodene (excluded - Cyproterone). F. Pill break - maximum 2 weeks continuously; pill breaks should not exceed 2 weeks consecutively (inactive pills not considered part of the pill break) and total pill breaks should not surpass 4 weeks within a 12-month period. Quantity must only allow continuation of OCP within the 2-year OCP review period. Pharmacists may charge a consultation fee for the service, in addition to the cost of OCP supplied. This is the protocol's single supply intervention (resupply of the patient's established OCP); the document does not rank products or alternatives - LARCs may be discussed with patients when appropriate. No product-level strengths/doses are printed in the extracted text; Attachment 1: Summary table for OCP (page 7) contains only its heading in the extraction.

open_questions.topic: Attachment 1 (Summary table for OCP) content is not present in the text extraction
open_questions.observed: Page 7 contains only the heading 'Attachment 1: Summary table for OCP' and the page number; no product rows, strengths, doses or quantities were extracted.
open_questions.why_unclear: No product-level treatment rows can be transcribed (strength/dose/frequency are left blank on TX-1) without inventing content; the table must be obtained from the source PDF or another route before product-level rules can be encoded.

open_questions.topic: Two-column K. Exclusion criteria table (COC vs POP) is interleaved in the text extraction
open_questions.observed: Page 2 prints 'Combined oral contraception (COC)' and 'Progestogen-only contraception (POP)' columns side by side; the extraction interleaves the two columns line by line. On page 2 the column assignment is recoverable from the interleaving pattern (e.g. 'Migraine with/without aura' and 'Prolonged immobilisation' are left/COC; 'Ischaemic heart disease, stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA) that develops during use of POP' is right/POP). Page 3 bullets have no visible column header and appear to continue the left (COC) column, but this cannot be confirmed from the extraction alone.
open_questions.why_unclear: Column tags were added as editorial annotations: [COC] and [POP] on page 2 (high confidence), [COC (inferred, see open question)] on page 3 with confidence 'medium'. Spec rule 2 requires ambiguous/misaligned table rows to be marked and recorded rather than reconciled silently.

open_questions.topic: Table note 'conditions that require immediate referral' has a cut-off subject
open_questions.observed: The right-hand notes column of the K. Exclusion criteria table reads: 'conditions that require immediate referral. Refer the patient to their regular GP with a copy of the assessment.' The subject (which conditions) is not legible in the extraction; from the layout it sits alongside the breast cancer and liver tumour rows.
open_questions.why_unclear: Captured as RF-1 with confidence 'unclear' and exact wording; the attachment of the note to specific rows cannot be confirmed from the text extraction.

open_questions.topic: Combinatorics of the scope criteria and exclusion list are inferred, not explicitly stated
open_questions.observed: The document lists criteria A-K as 'Program Scope WA criteria' without saying 'all' or 'any'. Supporting language: 'The resupply of OCP is permitted for TGD individuals, provided all other protocol conditions are met' (p.4) and 'provided other protocol conditions are met' (p.4) imply AND for the scope criteria; the K list is introduced as 'Exclusion criteria: ... Including UKMEC Category 3 & 4 contraindications, and ...' where presence of any item is a contraindication, implying OR.
open_questions.why_unclear: Scope criteria INC-1..INC-9 default to all_of and exclusions default to any_of; the document does not state combinatorics explicitly, so the mapping is inferred and recorded here per spec rule 4.

open_questions.topic: on_fail actions for pathway gates are partly derived
open_questions.observed: The document states referral for ineligibility ('Patients who have requested the service but are not eligible for resupply should be referred to their regular medical practitioner or health service', p.1), for age outside 16-39 (p.4) and for UKMEC category 3/4 risks (p.5), so those gates use on_fail 'REFER'. The document does not state what happens if consent is not obtained, if quantity conditions cannot be met, or if the review date cannot be verified.
open_questions.why_unclear: Those gates use on_fail 'unclear' per spec rule 5; the consequence must be confirmed rather than assumed.

open_questions.topic: STI screening appears both as an exclusion and as something that does not prevent resupply
open_questions.observed: 'STI screening is indicated (although OCP may still be resupplied by the pharmacist)' is listed in BOTH the COC and POP exclusion columns (p.2).
open_questions.why_unclear: Captured verbatim as EXC-8 and its parenthetical as exclusion exception EXE-1; the document gives no decision rule for when resupply proceeds versus when it does not (it does state 'STI screening is recommended for anyone who is sexually active and engaging in unprotected sex', p.6).

open_questions.observed: Referral wording appears on page 1 (not eligible), page 2 (table note), page 4 (age, medical review), page 5 (frequently takes pill breaks; refer confidentially) and page 6 (consent and destination).
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec rule for the referral block: one shared provenance object uses the first page of the range (page 2); the full range 2-6 is recorded here.

open_questions.observed: The document uses 'immediate referral' (p.2, captured in referral.urgent and RF-1) but never mentions emergency services, ambulance, 000 or emergency department.
open_questions.why_unclear: referral.emergency is empty because the source is silent; this reflects the document rather than an extraction gap.

open_questions.topic: notifiable captures My Health Record transmission and record sharing, not a notifiable condition
open_questions.observed: The document requires My Health Record upload of the dispensing record (with a documented patient request to withhold as a justifiable reason for not meeting condition 4(m) of the SASA) and provision of a copy of the record to the patient and, if necessary, their regular medical practitioner (p.5). No notifiable condition, AIR notification or compulsory GP notification is mentioned.
open_questions.why_unclear: notifiable.required is set true only for those explicitly printed transmission/sharing obligations; no public-health notification requirement exists in this document.

open_questions.topic: No version number or date printed
open_questions.observed: Page 1 carries only the title 'Pharmacist Resupply of Oral Contraceptive Pills Pilot - Western Australian Protocol'; no version, date, document identifier or approval line appears on any of the 7 pages (page 7 is the Attachment 1 heading).
open_questions.why_unclear: instrument_version and effective_date cannot be populated from the document.
